overview: Moldova is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, between Romania and Ukraine. Its capital is Chișinău. Moldova became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991, and its official language is Romanian. A strip of land east of the Dniester river, called Transnistria, has been controlled by a breakaway government since the early 1990s.

geography.text: Moldova is mostly gentle hills and plains with very fertile black soil, which makes it good farming country, especially for vineyards. The Prut river forms the border with Romania, and the Dniester runs through the east. Moldova has no mountains; its highest point is a hill only a few hundred metres high.

history.text: Much of today's Moldova was part of the medieval Principality of Moldavia, which later came under Ottoman control. Russia took its eastern half, called Bessarabia, in 1812. After a period as part of Romania between the World Wars, it became a Soviet republic, and in 1991 it declared independence. A short war in 1992 left Transnistria under a breakaway government.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: Russia takes Bessarabia from the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Soviet annexation
events.text: The Soviet Union takes the region.

government.text: Moldova is a parliamentary republic. The 101-member parliament chooses the Prime Minister, while the President is elected directly. Moldova became a candidate to join the European Union in 2022. Transnistria, a strip of land along the Ukrainian border, has been controlled by a breakaway government supported by Russia since 1992.

economy.text: Moldova is one of the poorest countries in Europe. Farming is very important, especially wine, fruit and walnuts, and many Moldovans work abroad and send money home. The country has worked to reduce its dependence on Russian gas.

culture.text: Most Moldovans speak Romanian, and the countries share much of their culture and history. Moldova has a long winemaking tradition: Mileștii Mici holds a huge wine collection in 200 kilometres of underground tunnels. Folk dances such as the hora are performed at celebrations.

items.title: Mileștii Mici
items.text: Underground wine cellars holding around 1.5 million bottles.

items.title: Orheiul Vechi
items.text: A cave monastery cut into a cliff above a river bend.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport in Moldova. Trântă, a traditional form of wrestling, is a national sport, and Moldovan athletes have won Olympic medals in wrestling, boxing and canoeing.

items.title: Trântă
items.text: Traditional belt wrestling, the national sport.
